attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I've poured days of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b08/review-experiment-tt2hghu_/call-f3d6c5ffe02a466986f9c8304aad29a5/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la && readlink -f manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(f'\\n===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout') for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))
print('Metadata:',r.metadata)
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('tmp/pdfs')
for pattern in ('page-*.txt', 'page-*.png', 'details-*.png', 'manuscript.txt'):
    for f in p.glob(pattern):
        f.unlink()
p.rmdir()
print('Removed temporary PDF inspection files.')
PY"

strengths: Significance: PreMIO addresses the useful setting of repeatedly solving related MIPs using historical solutions. Its cardinality constraints can be added through standard solver interfaces, and solving all four complementary regions preserves exactness when every subproblem is solved exactly.

Originality: Separate constraints on likely-zero and likely-one variables provide an interpretable way to tolerate aggregate prediction errors. Connecting their intercepts to uncertainty bounds is an intuitive design idea.

Evaluation: Experiments cover knapsack, set covering, and simulated unit commitment with both Gurobi and COPT under several heuristic settings. Figure 1 reports substantial time-to-target improvements, particularly for set covering, suggesting practical potential.

Presentation, limitations, and ethics: The high-level algorithm and instance-generation procedures are understandable. Remark 6 and Section 4.4 explicitly acknowledge imperfect probability estimates and infeasible predicted regions. No material ethical concerns are apparent from the described public and synthetic benchmarks. Source: :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b08/review-experiment-tt2hghu_/call-f3d6c5ffe02a466986f9c8304aad29a5/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}
weaknesses: Soundness: Theorem 2 is not justified under its stated assumptions. U and L depend on predictions for the same test instance, but Appendix B.4 applies Hoeffding using unconditional per-variable accuracies as though these were fixed groups. Independent correctness indicators need not retain those means after selection: with an all-zero optimum and independent false positives, U contains only errors despite high marginal accuracy. Appendix B.1 also incorrectly infers independence of test errors from independent training datasets by factoring an expectation over the shared instance parameter. These gaps undermine the central probabilistic justification.

Connection between theory and implementation: Theorem 3 assumes exact conditional means, whereas Section 4.1 uses logistic predictions without reporting calibration and permits a 10% optimality gap for large SCP training labels. No held-out measurements of calibration, error dependence, or optimal-solution retention establish that the theoretical guidance works as intended. Furthermore, delta = 0.8 in Section 4.2 certifies only a 20% lower bound on coverage for each inequality under the ideal assumptions; it does not certify high-probability containment.

Originality and comparative evidence: Comparisons are against the underlying commercial solvers, without directly evaluating closely related local branching [12] or prediction-distance constraints [11]. Comparisons using the same predictor, together with an ablation against a tuned cardinality radius, are needed to establish the added value of the particular constraints and concentration-based threshold selection.

Evaluation protocol: Section 4.2 measures time to reach a target selected retrospectively from PreMIO's own 120-second run, while the unrestricted solver receives 3600 seconds. This supports a specific time-to-target comparison, but there are no equal-budget objective gaps or primal-integral results, and handling of unreached targets is unclear. There are only five test instances per SCUC setting, with no uncertainty estimates or repeated-training analysis. Inclusion of prediction and preprocessing costs in the reported timings is also unclear.

Benchmark coverage: Section 4.4 retains 57 of 132 MIPLIB instances after excluding infeasible preferred regions and joint timeouts. The reported 16% improvement therefore establishes only conditional performance, without quantifying overall benefit including failures and fallback costs. Table 3 contains only 30 entries, including a duplicated blp-ar98 entry, so the stated 57-instance aggregate cannot be reconstructed.

Presentation and implementation guidance contain consequential inconsistencies. Appendix D defines alpha_L and alpha_U as prediction-error proportions but calls them accuracy and recommends maximizing them; its tau = 0.1 example also falls outside Theorem 3's stated range. Section 3.2 reverses the pruning condition: if the preferred region excludes all global optima, another region remains feasible under its incumbent cutoff. Even containing an optimum does not generally make the complementary LP relaxations infeasible.

Reproducibility: No code or generated-instance release is specified, and solver versions, logistic-regression fitting and regularization settings, and random seeds are insufficiently documented. Numerical reporting also needs reconciliation: applying the stated shifted geometric mean with shift 10 to Table 1's ten displayed left-panel instances gives approximately 36.6 seconds for Original and 32.1 seconds for PreMIO, rather than the reported 28.7 and 25.8 seconds.
